questions.question: What giant animals lived on Earth a long, long time ago before people?
questions.explanation: Dinosaurs were giant reptiles that lived millions of years ago.
questions.funFact: The word 'dinosaur' actually means 'terrible lizard'!

questions.question: In ancient Egypt, people built giant triangle-shaped buildings. What are they called?
questions.explanation: The ancient Egyptians built massive pyramids as tombs for their kings.
questions.funFact: The Great Pyramid is so big it was built with over 2 million stone blocks!

questions.question: A long time ago in Europe, kings and queens lived in big, strong buildings called what?
questions.explanation: Castles were built with tall stone walls to keep the people inside safe.
questions.funFact: Some castles had a 'moat' – a big ditch filled with water all around it!

questions.question: Before cars were invented, what animal did people ride to travel fast?
questions.explanation: People rode horses or had horses pull wagons to travel from place to place.
questions.funFact: Horses can sleep both lying down and standing up!

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong traveled in a spaceship and walked on the moon in 1969.
questions.funFact: His footprints are still on the moon today because there is no wind to blow them away!

questions.question: What is the really, really long wall in Asia that you can see from far away?
questions.explanation: The Great Wall of China was built a long time ago to protect the country.
questions.funFact: The Great Wall is actually made of many different walls joined together, and it's over 13,000 miles long!

questions.question: Before people had electric lights, what did they use to see in the dark?
questions.explanation: People used candles made of wax and string to light up their homes at night.
questions.funFact: Some people used to tell time using 'candle clocks' that burned down to certain marks!

questions.question: A long time ago, brave sailors called Vikings traveled the ocean in what?
questions.explanation: Vikings built special wooden boats called longships that were very fast.
questions.funFact: Viking longships often had the head of a scary dragon carved on the front!

questions.question: Where did some of the very first people draw pictures of animals?
questions.explanation: Early humans painted amazing pictures of animals on the walls of deep caves.
questions.funFact: Some of these cave paintings are over 40,000 years old!

questions.question: In ancient Rome, people gathered in a huge circle building to watch games. What is it called?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum was a massive amphitheater where Romans watched big events.
questions.funFact: They sometimes filled the bottom of the Colosseum with water to have pretend boat battles!

questions.question: What important round invention helps cars, bikes, and wagons roll?
questions.explanation: The wheel is one of the most important inventions in history for moving things.
questions.funFact: The oldest known wheel was actually used for making pottery, not for transportation!

questions.question: In ancient Japan, brave warriors wore cool armor and carried swords. Who were they?
questions.explanation: Samurai were highly respected warriors in Japan who followed a strict code of honor.
questions.funFact: Samurai armor was made of tiny metal plates tied together with colorful silk cords!

questions.question: A long time ago, people invented the first way to fly in the sky using what?
questions.explanation: Before airplanes, people used giant balloons filled with hot air to float up into the sky.
questions.funFact: The very first passengers in a hot air balloon were a sheep, a duck, and a rooster!

questions.question: In ancient Greece, people started a big sports competition that we still do today. What is it?
questions.explanation: The Olympic Games started in Greece with running, jumping, and throwing contests.
questions.funFact: Winners in the ancient Olympics didn't get gold medals; they got crowns made of olive leaves!

questions.question: A beautiful white marble building in India was built by an emperor for his wife. What is it?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal is a famous and beautiful monument in India.
questions.funFact: The white marble of the Taj Mahal changes color depending on the sun, looking pink in the morning and golden at night!

questions.question: Old-fashioned trains puff a lot of smoke because they were powered by what?
questions.explanation: Early trains used coal to boil water and make steam, which pushed the train forward.
questions.funFact: These old trains were often called 'Iron Horses'!

questions.question: Instead of writing with pens and pencils, ancient Egyptians wrote with pictures called what?
questions.explanation: Hieroglyphs were small pictures of birds, eyes, and lines that meant words and sounds.
questions.funFact: They wrote on a special kind of paper made from reeds called papyrus!

questions.question: Who were the people that sailed ships with black flags and looked for buried treasure?
questions.explanation: Pirates sailed the seas a long time ago, looking for gold and treasure.
questions.funFact: Many pirates wore an eye patch not because they lost an eye, but to keep one eye ready to see in the dark under the ship's deck!

questions.question: Long ago, Native American tribes living on the plains lived in cone-shaped tents called what?
questions.explanation: Teepees were warm and could be easily packed up when the tribe needed to move.
questions.funFact: The smoke from their fires would escape through a hole at the very top of the teepee!

questions.question: Before we had refrigerators, how did people keep their food cold?
questions.explanation: People had 'iceboxes' and the 'iceman' would bring huge blocks of frozen ice to their houses.
questions.funFact: The ice was cut from frozen lakes and rivers during the winter and saved for the summer!
